contexts.text: Empty scientifics... are like crustaceans or scaly things, which separate themselves spontaneously.
The names and words (in the Word) are like... scales, which fall down when they enter Heaven.
Interior natural things were signified by the excrescences (of the face) such as the hairs and scales of the skin: things from the Natural as to good, by the hairs, and... as to truth, by the scales.
The discourse (of such) is like a husk and chaff, relatively to the kernels.
Scientifics... without good in them, are nothing but scales among the dirt, which fall off.
Scales () = those things which are completely external, thus sensuous things, to which scientifics which are false adhere.

The truths which descend from such a principle, adhere to the surface; and, when they are being vastated, they fall off like scales, leaving stinking places, from the falsities which exhale from the evils there.
The moral things of their life (here) then become like the scales of fishes, which are wiped off.
Its body (appeared) like a scaly fish... because a scaly fish is sensuous scientifics.
Such (useless matters of learning) are like scales upon scales, which grow on and make dense the outer skin, and take away the sense for interior things.
In the sensuous man... there are fallacies and derivative falsities, which is signified by that the fish shall adhere to the scales of the whale ().
Scales () = the fallacies of the senses, which ar-e scientifics of the lowest sort.
